title: Individual characteristics outperform resting-state fMRI for the prediction of behavioral phenotypes.
summary: Predictive models on 20,000 UK Biobank participants found demographic characteristics outperformed resting-fMRI features for four behavioral phenotypes, while fMRI added some predictive information.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models comparing demographic and resting-fMRI predictors of behavior
organization: Institute of Neuroscience and Medicine; Research Center Jülich; Institute of Systems Neuroscience; Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf

evidence.tested: Held-out predictive comparisons support relative prediction in the UK Biobank sample; they do not imply causal neural mechanisms.
evidence.unknown: The UK Biobank prediction results do not establish causal neural mechanisms or prediction in other populations.
evidence.ai_role: Compares predictive value of demographic characteristics and resting-state fMRI for four behavioral phenotypes in 20,000 UK Biobank participants.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
